newsitem.title: INDIA: Lehman sees Indian economy recovering strongly.
newsitem.headline: Lehman sees Indian economy recovering strongly.

text.p: Global investment bank Lehman Brothers on Thursday recommended investors to go overweight in Indian market as it saw a strong economic recovery emerging.
The firm forecast the Bombay Stock Exchange's top-30 share index to reach 3,900 points by December.
The benchmark index was trading at 3,498.59, off 27.38 points or 0.78 percent, on Thursday afternoon.

"Lehman Brothers predicts a strong economic recovery and advises moving selectively away from stable sectors towards cyclicals such as cement and construction," the firm said in a statement quoting its research report titled "Turning positive on Indian cyclicals".
It expects India's industrial output to grow nine percent in fiscal 1996/97 (April-March) and by 11 percent in 1997/98.
The report said cement shares had underperformed the market for the past year by more than 30 percentage points while construction had lagged by 45 percentage points.

"Given that infrastructure remains a key focus for the government, and that the formation of the fund dedicated to the development of infrastructure is expected in the near future, the report favours engineering and construction sectors while selectively adding to cement stocks," the statement said.
The firm has increased its weighting of Gujarat Ambuja Cement, Larsen & Toubro and Indian Hotels -- and lowered that of Hindustan Lever and Mahanagar Telephone Nigam.
"Recovery in earnings for cyclicals ... (would) be selective rather than sector-wide, and muted rather than robust," it quoted chief equity strategist Abhijit Chakrabortti as saying.
Chakrabortti remains skeptical about price performance in sectors vulnerable to global commodity cycles, the statement said.
